refinement_notes: Reduced from 25 to 22 archetypes through 3 strategic merges based on correlation analysis and conceptual overlap

archetypes.name: Anti-Displacement Advocate
archetypes.description: Community stability, anti-displacement, racial equity, skeptical of market-rate development
core_values: Community stability and anti-displacement as top priorities
Racial justice and reparations for displacement
typical_concerns: Luxury apartments pricing out existing residents
Loss of cultural community character and small businesses
priorities: 100% affordable housing projects and community land trusts
Strong tenant protections and rent control
Community benefits agreements and local hire

differentiators.vs_housing_champion: Strongly opposed to market-rate development even with affordability requirements
differentiators.vs_housing_rights_advocate: More focused on preventing displacement than expanding tenant rights
differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: Equity-focused not aesthetic, frames preservation through racial justice lens

archetypes.merge_rationale: r=0.902 correlation, 76% agreement. Both focused on preventing displacement with slight framing differences (racial equity vs. general anti-displacement). Merge preserves both concerns.

archetypes.name: Community Builder
archetypes.description: Social cohesion, public spaces, community programs
core_values: Strong social ties and community cohesion
Public spaces as gathering places for all
typical_concerns: Social isolation and declining civic participation
priorities: Parks, community centers, and public spaces
Support for local businesses and institutions

differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: More inclusive of newcomers and diversity

archetypes.name: Direct Democracy Proponent
archetypes.description: Ballot measures, participatory budgeting, direct voting
core_values: Direct citizen control over major decisions
Distrust of elected officials and insiders
typical_concerns: Lack of meaningful public input in decisions

differentiators.vs_community_builder: Formal democratic structures not informal community

archetypes.name: Environmental Steward
archetypes.description: Climate action, conservation, sustainability, environmental justice
core_values: Climate crisis requires urgent government action
Conservation of natural resources and biodiversity
Sustainable development balancing growth and ecology
typical_concerns: Carbon emissions from buildings and transportation
Tree removal and habitat loss from development
Pollution in low-income communities and communities of color
priorities: Tree preservation ordinances and urban forestry

differentiators.vs_transit_advocate: More cautious about development impacts on trees/habitat
differentiators.vs_green_new_dealer: Less focused on jobs program, more on conservation
differentiators.vs_housing_champion: May oppose housing if environmental impacts are significant

archetypes.name: Family & Education Advocate
archetypes.description: Schools, family services, childcare, educational equity, child safety
core_values: Quality public education and well-funded schools
Educational equity and support for all children
typical_concerns: Lack of affordable childcare and family services
Unsafe streets and inadequate child-friendly infrastructure
priorities: Increased school funding and teacher compensation
Universal pre-K and affordable childcare programs
Safe Routes to School and family-friendly design

differentiators.vs_senior_services_advocate: Focuses on children and families rather than older adults
differentiators.vs_community_builder: Specifically focused on education and family services, not general community programs
differentiators.vs_safety_first: Child safety through infrastructure and services, not just law enforcement

archetypes.merge_rationale: Conceptual overlap - parents primarily concerned with education and child services. Education advocates focus on schools and youth programs. Merge captures family-oriented civic priorities comprehensively.

archetypes.name: Fiscal Conservative
archetypes.description: Limited government, low taxes, fiscal responsibility
core_values: Private sector efficiency over public programs
priorities: Pension reform and privatization where feasible

differentiators.vs_market_urbanist: May support zoning restrictions to protect property values
differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: Less focused on character, more on fiscal impacts

archetypes.name: Government Watchdog
archetypes.description: Transparency, accountability, ethics, good governance
core_values: Open data and public records access
priorities: Open data portals and financial transparency

differentiators.vs_fiscal_conservative: Focuses on process and ethics not ideology

real_world_examples: Local investigative journalists and civic watchdogs

archetypes.name: Green New Dealer
archetypes.description: Climate action through government jobs programs and investment
core_values: Climate crisis requires massive public investment
Green jobs and union labor in climate transition
Environmental justice and economic justice are inseparable
Government as driver of clean energy transformation
typical_concerns: Fossil fuel industry blocking climate action
Job losses in carbon-intensive industries without alternatives
Private sector insufficient for climate response
priorities: Public green jobs programs (weatherization, solar installation)
Public transit and EV charging infrastructure
Just transition for fossil fuel workers

differentiators.vs_environmental_steward: More focused on jobs and economic transformation
differentiators.vs_labor_organizer: Climate is central priority, not just working conditions
differentiators.vs_techno_optimist: Skeptical of private sector tech solutions

real_world_examples: Democratic Socialists of America ecosocialist working groups

archetypes.name: Homeowner Stability Seeker
archetypes.description: Property values, Prop 13, neighborhood stability
core_values: Homeownership as wealth building and security
typical_concerns: Property tax increases threatening fixed incomes
Density bringing traffic and parking problems

differentiators.vs_renter_advocate: Opposite sides on rent control and tenant rights
differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: More focused on property values than aesthetics

archetypes.name: Housing Champion
archetypes.description: Pro-housing across income levels, supports density and development
core_values: Housing abundance as solution to affordability crisis
Economic and racial integration through mixed-income neighborhoods
Market-rate and affordable housing are complementary
typical_concerns: Severe housing shortage driving displacement and homelessness
priorities: Upzoning near transit and jobs centers
Streamlined permitting for all housing types
Inclusionary requirements paired with density bonuses
By-right development to reduce discretionary approvals

differentiators.vs_slow_growth_advocate: Supports market-rate development with affordability requirements, not just 100% affordable
differentiators.vs_market_urbanist: More willing to accept government regulation and affordability mandates
differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: Prioritizes regional housing supply over neighborhood character preservation

archetypes.name: Housing Rights Advocate
archetypes.description: Housing as human right, tenant protections, social housing, anti-commodification
core_values: Housing as human right requiring public provision and strong protections
Tenant rights, rent control, and anti-eviction protections
Social housing model (Vienna, Singapore) as alternative to market
Renter power in housing policy and community control
typical_concerns: Housing treated as commodity not human right
Weak tenant protections and arbitrary evictions
Landlord power and real estate speculation
priorities: Social housing programs modeled on Vienna, Singapore
Strong rent control and just-cause eviction laws
Tenant organizing and renter power in policy
Public land trusts and community ownership

differentiators.vs_housing_champion: Opposes market-rate development, supports only public/social housing
differentiators.vs_anti_displacement_advocate: More focused on tenant rights and public housing than preventing displacement
differentiators.vs_market_urbanist: Rejects market solutions, believes housing requires public provision

archetypes.merge_rationale: r=0.807 correlation, 63% agreement. Both progressive housing advocates with different emphases (tenant protections vs. social housing). Merge creates comprehensive housing rights perspective.

archetypes.name: Justice Reformer
archetypes.description: Criminal justice reform, police accountability, alternatives to incarceration
core_values: Racial justice and ending mass incarceration
Mental health and social services over criminalization
Root causes of crime (poverty, trauma, lack of opportunity)
typical_concerns: Police violence and lack of accountability
Over-policing of Black and Brown communities
Criminalization of homelessness and mental illness
priorities: Mental health crisis response teams (not police)
Independent police oversight with real power

differentiators.vs_safety_first: Sees over-policing as problem, not solution
differentiators.vs_community_builder: Explicitly focused on criminal justice reform

real_world_examples: Communities United for Restorative Youth Justice (CURYJ)

archetypes.name: Labor Organizer
archetypes.description: Worker rights, living wages, unions, labor standards
core_values: Living wages and benefits for all
priorities: Living wage ordinances and prevailing wage
Project labor agreements and union hiring

archetypes.name: Market Urbanist
archetypes.description: Libertarian YIMBY: pro-density, anti-regulation, market solutions
core_values: Minimal government regulation of housing market
Property rights and freedom to build
Filtering theory (new luxury housing frees up older stock)
priorities: Eliminate zoning entirely or allow by-right development
Remove parking minimums and setback requirements
Market-rate development as primary affordability solution

differentiators.vs_housing_champion: Opposes affordability mandates and government intervention
differentiators.vs_fiscal_conservative: Supports density even if it changes neighborhood character
differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: Opposes all zoning restrictions including historic preservation

archetypes.name: Neighborhood Protector
archetypes.description: Character preservation, anti-density, local control
typical_concerns: Loss of historic buildings and trees

archetypes.name: Pragmatic Incrementalist
archetypes.description: Evidence-based policy, pilot programs, gradual reform
core_values: Evidence and data drive good policy
real_world_examples: Policy wonks and urban planning professionals

archetypes.name: Regional Thinker
archetypes.description: Regional coordination, metropolitan perspective, systems thinking
core_values: Equitable distribution of benefits and burdens
typical_concerns: Concentration of affordable housing in few cities

differentiators.vs_housing_champion: Broader than housing, includes all regional systems

real_world_examples: SPUR (San Francisco Bay Area Planning and Urban Research)

archetypes.name: Safety First
archetypes.description: Public safety, law enforcement, emergency services
core_values: Public safety as fundamental government responsibility
Strong law enforcement and emergency response
Order and security for families and businesses
typical_concerns: Rising crime rates and property crime
Drug use and disorder in public spaces

differentiators.vs_justice_reformer: Supports traditional law enforcement over alternatives
differentiators.vs_fiscal_conservative: Willing to spend on public safety
differentiators.vs_community_builder: Security through enforcement not social programs

archetypes.name: Senior Services Advocate
archetypes.description: Senior services, accessibility, healthcare, fixed income concerns
core_values: Dignity and independence for older adults
typical_concerns: Rising costs threatening seniors on fixed incomes
Lack of accessible housing and transit
priorities: Senior tax exemptions and rent protections
Healthcare clinics and home care support

differentiators.vs_fiscal_conservative: Supports social services and tax exemptions
differentiators.vs_homeowner_stability_seeker: Social services not just property concerns

real_world_examples: Area Agencies on Aging advisory councils

archetypes.name: Small Business Booster
archetypes.description: Local businesses, entrepreneurship, downtown vitality
typical_concerns: Regulations and fees burdening small businesses

differentiators.vs_fiscal_conservative: Supports targeted business subsidies and interventions
differentiators.vs_market_urbanist: May support regulations to protect small business

archetypes.name: Techno-Optimist
archetypes.description: Smart cities, data-driven governance, technology solutions
core_values: Technology as solution to civic challenges
typical_concerns: Analog processes when digital solutions exist
Resistance to innovation and new approaches

archetypes.name: Transit Advocate
archetypes.description: Public transit expansion, car-free living, transit-oriented development
core_values: Public transit as backbone of sustainable cities
Transit equity and access for all income levels
priorities: Light rail, BRT, and frequent bus service expansion
Protected bike lanes and pedestrian infrastructure

differentiators.vs_environmental_steward: More willing to accept development trade-offs for transit
differentiators.vs_housing_champion: Transit access is prerequisite for density support
differentiators.vs_neighborhood_protector: Supports road diets and parking removal
